data.title: Macron convenes French party leaders as soaring energy prices put focus on wars in Iran and Ukraine
data.description: Haxie Meyers-Belkin is pleased to welcome Renaud Foucart, Senior Lecturer in Economics at Lancaster University’s Management School in the UK. data.title: ‘We’ve been on a good run lately. We’ve not had a row for weeks!’: Coleen and Wayne Rooney on marriage, mistakes and making reality TV
data.description: His on-pitch triumphs (and off-pitch scandals), her turn as Wagatha Christie … for years, the football power couple have made headlines, despite efforts to keep their lives private. So why are they now about to reveal all on screen? “If you’d said to me 10 years ago, ‘You’re going to be doing a TV show about the family’, I would have said, ‘No chance’,” Wayne Rooney says. Few would have disagreed. After all, he and his wife Coleen had spent their adult lifetime running away from the public gaze. And not very successfully, at that. Wayne, a wonderful footballer with the strength of a bull and agility of an acrobat, was often back-page news. He scored 253 goals for Manchester United (overtaking Bobby Charlton’s record), 53 for England (the record until Harry Kane surpassed him in 2023), is still England’s youngest goal scorer (17 years and 317 days), won five Premier League titles, was twice young player of the year and was voted player of the year by both his peers and football journalists in 2009/10. Continue reading...

data.title: Burning forests, emptying rivers, €180bn in damage: Europe’s politicians face reckoning after ‘summer of truth’
data.description: Amid record-shattering heatwaves and popular demand for climate action, why are politicians often timid or in denial? It was, according to the European Commission president, Ursula von der Leyen, the “summer of truth” . Climate chaos ripped through Europe and the northern hemisphere, sending heat records tumbling, scorching crops in the fields, burning forests, emptying rivers and reservoirs, warping train tracks, melting roads and killing about 35,000 people in Europe alone. The EU has estimated the damage at about €180bn, and the full bill is yet to arrive: harvests have been depleted, which will probably raise food price inflation, and expensive repairs to infrastructure have only just begun. Continue reading...

data.title: The Guide #261: There is so much good telly this autumn you may never go outside again
data.description: In this week’s newsletter: From HBO’s incredible divorce drama War to the hilarious return of The Paper, there’s too much TV to choose from even for a confirmed addict like me For those of us who like to stay indoors, it has been a bad summer. The World Cup ate up all traditional television scheduling, and the streamers apparently declined to counterprogramme. The Bear came and went before anybody noticed, and House of the Dragon conclusively disappeared up its own bottom. If you’re anything like me then you clung to the good stuff (basically Disney’s Furious and nothing else) like a life raft, eking out new episodes like someone in a desert sucking condensation off the underside of a tarpaulin. But forget summer. It is now autumn, and television is back. In fact, I can’t remember a time when television has come roaring back with quite the same ferocity as it has this month. data.title: US and Denmark reach security deal after Trump’s threats to take over Greenland
data.description: The agreement would allow the US to expand its military presence, while Denmark and Greenland say it preserves their sovereignty and right to self-determination Donald Trump announced on Friday that the US had struck an Arctic security pact with the leaders of Denmark and Greenland, after threatening for much of his second term to annex the semi-autonomous Danish territory by force. The full scope of the deal Trump described as “very important, historic, and special” was not immediately clear. But soon after his announcement in a post on Truth Social, the leaders of Denmark and Greenland issued statements indicating the deal would be signed by the three governments on the sidelines of the United Nations general assembly in New York City next week. data.title: Jonathan Franzen: ‘It’s still mysterious to me that I was angry for so long’
data.description: The author of The Corrections talks about a new TV adaptation, the future of reading and why creating new work is ‘horrible’ When HBO dropped its plan to adapt Jonathan Franzen’s bestselling novel The Corrections in 2012, the author was so relieved he says he performed his first and last cartwheel on the lawn of his home in Santa Cruz, California. There had been an attempted film adaptation before that, but he had been unsurprised by its failure, having warned that it was impossible to condense his densely plotted doorstopper of a novel into a feature-length film. This time, Franzen had signed up as co-writer, with filmmaker Noah Baumbach. He says that HBO was “excluded from the development process. Mistake, because we didn’t know how to do TV.” Franzen himself hadn’t even owned a telly until a few years earlier and certainly didn’t have cable, so as he was wrestling with the script, he began renting box sets. Around three episodes into one drama series, he realised “we have no idea what we’re doing. This is not how you do TV. This is bad,” he recalls. The result, he says, was “one of the worst pilots anyone has ever made”. Franzen used to think TV was the “enemy” of the serious novelist. In a well-known 1996 essay for Harper’s Magazine about the decline of high literature he had complained bitterly about the “banal ascendancy of television”. But after the HBO series failed, he watched Breaking Bad, Nurse Jackie and Silicon Valley and loved them. In the age of social media, AI and the endless scroll, TV has started to look like a “friend”, he says now. And The Corrections is finally being adapted into an eight-part Netflix series, with Meryl Streep playing Enid Lambert, the matriarch clinging to dreams of hosting a perfect last family Christmas, even as her husband Alfred is in terminal decline with Parkinson’s and dementia and their grownup children’s lives are falling apart in terrible, comical ways. Once Streep announced she was in, Franzen felt the “chances of making this show have gone up above 50%”. He says he’s a month away from finishing the script. Continue reading...
data.translatedTitle: Jonathan Franzen: ‘It’s still mysterious to me that I was angry for so long’
data.translatedDescription: The author of The Corrections talks about a new TV adaptation, the future of reading and why creating new work is ‘horrible’ When HBO dropped its plan to adapt Jonathan Franzen’s bestselling novel The Corrections in 2012, the author was so relieved he says he performed his first and last cartwheel on the lawn of his home in Santa Cruz, California. There had been an attempted film adaptation before that, but he had been unsurprised by its failure, having warned that it was impossible to condense his densely plotted doorstopper of a novel into a feature-length film. This time, Franzen had signed up as co-writer, with filmmaker Noah Baumbach. He says that HBO was “excluded from the development process. Mistake, because we didn’t know how to do TV.” Franzen himself hadn’t even owned a telly until a few years earlier and certainly didn’t have cable, so as he was wrestling with the script, he began renting box sets. Around three episodes into one drama series, he realised “we have no idea what we’re doing. This is not how you do TV. This is bad,” he recalls. The result, he says, was “one of the worst pilots anyone has ever made”. Franzen used to think TV was the “enemy” of the serious novelist. In a well-known 1996 essay for Harper’s Magazine about the decline of high literature he had complained bitterly about the “banal ascendancy of television”. But after the HBO series failed, he watched Breaking Bad, Nurse Jackie and Silicon Valley and loved them. In the age of social media, AI and the endless scroll, TV has started to look like a “friend”, he says now. And The Corrections is finally being adapted into an eight-part Netflix series, with Meryl Streep playing Enid Lambert, the matriarch clinging to dreams of hosting a perfect last family Christmas, even as her husband Alfred is in terminal decline with Parkinson’s and dementia and their grownup children’s lives are falling apart in terrible, comical ways. Once Streep announced she was in, Franzen felt the “chances of making this show have gone up above 50%”. He says he’s a month away from finishing the script. Continue reading...

data.title: Youth: Sharon Horgan’s comedy about dating at 50 is utterly hilarious
data.description: The perils of ageing and the horrors of finding post-divorce romance are laid bare in the new show from the creator of Motherland. It’s humungously funny, and so acutely observed it’s painful Ageing has changed, hasn’t it? There’s a generation of middle-aged and perimenopausal elder millennials and xennials who refuse to do it. We’re young enough to be part of an online world that puts a premium on appearance, too old for such narcissistic self-branding to be achieved without unsustainable effort. Dating apps and social media connect people across generations, so it’s easy to become confused about how old we actually are. Here’s a tip: ask your knees. This brings us to Youth (from Monday 21 September, HBO Max), Sharon Horgan ’s dramedy about being 50. That perky title is a quip about the decade being known as “the youth of old age”. Horgan is Alex, a divorcee in her sandwich years, caring for teenage son Ruarí and ageing parents. There’s a lot going on in her life, and some doom. She’s falling forwards in a semi-successful career as a literary agent, getting back into dating under pressure. She needs someone to fall in love with her immediately, as she points out to her best friend. Not for romantic myth-making, but “so there’s a bit of time with the present version of me, before the ‘old me’ is here”. Continue reading...

data.title: Brentford blitz Chelsea as Fábio Carvalho caps stunning second-half display
data.description: Those early-season thoughts that Chelsea might be the team best-placed to challenge Arsenal are beginning to look extremely over-optimistic. The two chaotic wins with which they began were always difficult to read: they might have been useful points picked up on the way to a more solid structure, or they might have represented evidence of significant problems. After three games without a win, and 12 goals conceded in five games this season, it’s beginning to look like the latter. At the final whistle, Keith Andrews tipped his head back and roared at the sky, celebrating Brentford’s first home win over Chelsea since 1938. They remain unbeaten, coherent and disciplined, and moved up to third in the table. The comparison is impossible not to draw: as one side flail in an orgy of structured spending, their far less wealthy neighbours thrive with a clear plan and sense of direction. “It was a performance I felt was bubbling,” said Andrews. “I could see it in the players’ eyes over the last two days. They were very focused, very determined.” Continue reading...

data.title: Harry Kane smashes record for fastest to 100 Bundesliga goals in 98th game
data.description: Kane double helps Bayern Munich beat Union Berlin 7-0 Dieter Müller’s record of 129 games had stood since 1977 Harry Kane smashed the 49-year-old record for the fastest player to score 100 Bundesliga goals in Bayern Munich’s 7-0 victory over Union Berlin, his 98th league game for the club. Cologne’s Dieter Müller set the previous mark in 1977, but it took him 129 matches and, with the England captain scoring at better than a goal a game, a new record had been inevitable for some time. Since his arrival in 2023 Kane had been averaging a Bundesliga goal every 78.5 minutes and has now scored 152 in 154 appearances in all competitions, including 61 in 51 games last term. The director of football, Jason Wilcox, looked unamused on his way out of the directors’ box but he and the hierarchy need to accept responsibility for their actions. This is the natural course of football, where supporters know what is good or bad and give a rapid opinion to those whose wages they deem they pay. data.title: We wanted to let Max Dowman bloom in the shadows but he has become hard to ignore | Barney Ronay
data.description: This most modern and well-honed of footballers will not be able to escape the spotlight in an age of constant scrutiny but looks equipped to handle it The poet Jorge Luis Borges wrote a famous short story about a society that had become so good at making maps, so obsessed with capturing every detail, that its rulers decided the only way to do the job right was to make a lifesize map of its entire empire, which could then be laid out across the actual land from coast to coast. Imagine a map of Britain the exact same size as Britain, showing every branch of Greggs, every nail bar, every vape shop in perfect detail. Only then can we really see what Britain looks like, by standing on a fake Britain laid over the top of actual Britain. Borges was writing in the 1940s, at a time when people were fascinated by the mechanised future, with its new forms of measuring out the world: the wireless, the 30mph motorcar, the rise of Big Tape Measure. And to be fair, the mega-map is a pretty accurate vision of our own fully networked present, a place where you can snoop around a village in Mozambique from your laptop in Egham, where no one ever stops committing acts of minute self-surveillance, even if they think they’re just searching “What is beetroot?” on the internet. Continue reading...

data.title: ‘Embrace the chaos’: Tuchel aims to harness England’s football culture
data.description: Head coach says he must accept lack of control in games ‘Deep down, English players … they go for it’ Thomas Tuchel has admitted there are times when he craves greater control in matches. But the England head coach feels the more chaotic, adrenaline-fuelled nature of the Premier League will remain his template as he targets glory at Euro 2028. Tuchel described his team as “maybe not the most economical to play football” in terms of their habit of constantly playing at full throttle. They lost to Argentina in the World Cup semi-final in July when they had nothing left in the tank and watched the game slip away after going 1-0 up in the 55th minute. England barely touched the ball thereafter, had no control and were reeled in, Argentina winning with two late goals. Continue reading...

data.title: Uefa and Concacaf ask Gianni Infantino to give Fifa’s billions to its member associations
data.description: Payout of at least $10m to each association proposed Leaders want plan to be considered by Fifa Council The presidents of Uefa and Concacaf have written to Gianni Infantino requesting that Fifa release money from its $6bn (£4.5bn) reserves to its member associations, stating that the plan to fund them via the doomed Fifa Forward Enterprise scheme was unnecessary given the cash pile it is sitting on. Aleksander Ceferin and Victor Montagliani proposed a payout of at least $10m to each of Fifa’s 211 member associations (MAs), initially as a one-off during the 2027-2030 commercial cycle. They called for an independent review of Fifa’s financial position and said their own study “raises an important question as to whether the proposed transaction was necessary to deliver greater resources to the MAs”. Continue reading...

data.title: Here’s how Germany can defend its democracy – banning the AfD isn’t the answer | Timothy Garton Ash
data.description: Instead, constrain it legally and fight it politically. The world is watching Far-right nationalist populist parties are making the running everywhere from Washington to Warsaw. So why be so alarmed about a little regional electoral victory for one such party, the Alternative für Deutschland (AfD), in one federal state, Saxony-Anhalt? “Because it’s Germany!” is the almost instinctive answer in many heads around the world. But that “because it’s Germany” needs to be taken apart, like the segments of an orange. Yes, because of Adolf Hitler, two dictatorships (Nazi Germany until 1945, communist-ruled East Germany until 1989) and two world wars. And yes, some of the language used by the AfD will give anyone familiar with Nazi rhetoric a cold shudder down the spine. Timothy Garton Ash is a historian, political writer and Guardian columnist. His new book, Europe in 7 1/2 Chapters , is published in October Do you have an opinion on the issues raised in this article? data.title: Nine women in South Africa have been murdered since July. We are being told to be vigilant – but where are the warnings to men? | Nolethu Ndude
data.description: The country has one of the highest femicide rates in the world, and women are yet again being asked to remove themselves from public life to counter it When I heard the authorities advising women in and around Kempton Park, the site of a recent spate of femicides, not to walk or run alone, to avoid isolated places and to “remain vigilant”, my immediate response was anger. Remain vigilant. How groundbreaking. Women are already vigilant. We photograph number plates before entering vehicles. We share Uber details with friends. We phone one another while walking. We watch the driver’s route and notice every unexpected turn. We avoid certain roads, certain times and certain conversations. We scan parking areas before getting out of our cars. We check the back seat. We listen for footsteps. We carry pepper spray where we can. We hold our keys in a way that makes us feel slightly less defenceless. Continue reading...

data.title: After 20 years of my school dinners campaign, I’m a happy man. At last, we’re going to feed kids properly | Jamie Oliver
data.description: This week’s government announcement on school food standards is huge. It’s based on common sense and science. Beautiful! More than 20 years ago, when I started the campaign and TV series School Dinners , I couldn’t believe that we had standards for dog food but no standards for the food we fed our children at school. I have never, and will never, stop banging that drum – even after this week’s momentous announcement on school food standards in England. Because it is so important we remember where we started from. Children in the state sector are at school for 190 days a year. And if they’re eating breakfast and lunch there, the majority of what they consume each day is in the hands of their school. When we know that children are consuming less than half the recommended fruit and vegetables, but twice the recommended sugar , school food is a massive opportunity to directly improve diets at scale. data.title: This Israeli election could be the country’s last – this week I saw that for myself | Jonathan Freedland
data.description: Spend time on the ground and you see how high the stakes are for next month’s contest – for Israelis and Palestinians alike Candidates always say it, but this time it’s true. When Israel goes to the polls on 27 October , it really will be the most important election in the country’s history – and not just for Israelis. I saw that for myself this last week, in a visit that served as a sharp reminder of both what is at stake – and the role of those watching from afar. More than one voter I spoke to voiced the fear that, if the coalition headed by Benjamin Netanyahu is returned to power next month, 27 October will not merely be Israel’s most important election: it will be its last. They were not referring to the absence of democracy in the occupied territory of the West Bank – which we’ll come to – but rather to Israel’s internationally recognised, pre-1967 borders: what you might call Israel-proper. data.title: Earl Spencer SLATES the king. Charles DESTROYS Spencer. If only Diana were here to click on it | Marina Hyde
data.description: It’s a battle for hearts and minds – and TikTok, and the ’Gram. Just as it should be. #royalbeef Reading the extracts from Earl Spencer’s book about his sister Diana, and the king’s two-footed takedown of it , it’s hard to escape the idea that Spencer and the Windsors are just elite content creators now. This entire thing is basically indistinguishable from a blockbuster influencer war, and I honestly won’t be happy till the king puts out a shade TikTok of him driving round the Sandringham estate in sunglasses captioned: “Threatening to release the receipts but never actually releasing the receipts … kinda chic.” Soundtrack: Mariah Carey’s Obsessed. Meanwhile, perhaps trying to disguise his full descent into the algorithm mines, Charles Spencer has started talking like one of those adverts for twee porcelain plates that you used to see in magazine supplements. You know the kind of thing – “these three little kittens are waiting to steal your heart”. Here is the earl on his Diana book, which he has called Swan Song: “At heart, this is a brother’s simple tribute to an extraordinary sister.” Mmm. And simply bound, very simply, into paginated form as a precious, simple keepsake that also functions as one of Penguin Random House’s lead titles for autumn and the run-in to Christmas. Favourite charming tribute from today’s serialisation in the Mail? Probably the bit when Diana drags Spencer for lunch in the London restaurant San Lorenzo to announce: “My husband is in love with his valet”. Nkay. Continue reading...

data.title: The Guardian view on NAZA’s persecuted directors: journalism is not treason | Editorial
data.description: Politicians who threaten filmmakers rather than investigate alleged military crimes expose not strength but a leadership frightened of the evidence Across Israel, politicians, military leaders and much of the media are trying to discredit a documentary that almost none of them have seen. Produced by the Guardian, NAZA examines the AI-powered targeting systems used by the Israel Defense Forces to bombard Gaza after Hamas’s brutal 7 October 2023 attacks. Named after the Israeli military acronym euphemistically used for “collateral damage”, NAZA features interviews with 24 anonymous insiders who reflect on their role in the death-dealing. Israeli leaders have branded the film a “blood libel” and “fiction”. Its Oscar-winning directors, Rachel Szor and Yuval Abraham, face being stripped of their citizenship for treason. This is absurd. NAZA shows how bureaucratic distance and routine can turn extreme violence into ordinary work. More than 73,000 Palestinians, including more than 20,000 children, have been killed in the campaign by Israel’s military. A democracy that values life would at least investigate the film’s claims. Instead Israel’s government, which says it is committed to democratic accountability, is attacking journalists. Do you have an opinion on the issues raised in this article? data.title: Jay-Z in 8 review – the rapper’s interminable interview show should have been a podcast
data.description: Rick Rubin’s eight-part interview series with the MC is irritatingly unstructured, has portions that feel like filler and would hugely benefit from a different medium – which encourages use of the pause button Jay-Z in 8 does what it says on the can: the docuseries, released by Mubi, finds influential, mercurial superproducer Rick Rubin interviewing rap titan Jay-Z over the course of eight meandering, freeform episodes. Directed by Rubin himself and shot in black and white, the series is ostensibly designed to give viewers a look inside the brain of a godlike musical figure as he celebrates 30 years in music. As it makes eminently clear, this is a deeply reflective time for Jay-Z: in any given episode, he is liable to make reference to old collaborators such as Biggie and Jaz-O, reminisce on his upbringing in the Marcy Projects (the public housing units in Brooklyn where he grew up), and speak with astonishment about his rapid rise from crack dealer to generational rapper, often swinging between anecdotes with free-associative ease. Continue reading...

data.title: ‘The man’s a psychopath when it comes to hedgerows’: Derek vs Derek, the unexpectedly heartwarming doc about farmers at war
data.description: One Devon farmer, called Derek, is committed to rewilding his land. His neighbour, also a Derek, tends cattle and crops. What happened when a film-maker decided to follow the bickering pair? Derek Gow and Derek Banbury should hate each other. Gow is an outspoken rewilder widely credited with bringing back the beaver in England. As he returns his Devon sheep farm to wild nature, he is also breeding storks, wildcats, red-backed shrikes, glowworms and even adders to return to the countryside. Over the hedge, Banbury, his neighbour, is proud to be an intensive farmer, producing milk and beef cattle behind tightly clipped hedges. “It’s like he’s just gone mad,” says Banbury of Gow at the start of Derek vs Derek , an illuminating and unexpectedly funny new documentary that follows the pair over three years. “And the madness is now crossing the road on to my land.” Continue reading...

data.title: Phaedra Ensemble: The Music of Meredith Monk review – fleeting rough edges amid polished beauty
data.description: Kings Place, London Works by the not-quite-minimalist composer’s included her Realm Variations and quartet Stringsongs in a compelling concert There’s no one quite like Meredith Monk . So often grouped with her lionised contemporaries Philip Glass , Steve Reich , Terry Riley and La Monte Young , she is 83 to their 90-odd years and sports long plaited hair as reliably as Reich wears a baseball cap. Yet she refuses the label “minimalism” for her music, and composition is just one element of a creative life that also takes in singing, choreography, film-making and drawing. Monk was not present at this performance marking the launch of Phaedra Ensemble’s new album of her music , though she did loom briefly over the audience on video, professing “it’s a dream of mine for this music to be recorded and played”. data.title: Singapore is paying people to read books – can it fix the reading crisis?
data.description: A government scheme is giving citizens cash for spending time with a good book. We ask behavioural scientists, along with The Anxious Generation author and psychologist Jonathan Haidt, whether it’ll help make the habit stick Could the solution to the reading crisis lie in paying people to put down their phones and pick up a book? That’s what one government, at least, is resorting to: this month, Singapore launched a scheme promising actual cash to citizens as a reward for logging reading time on a government website. It’s unlikely to make you megabucks – you have to rack up 50 reading sessions of at least 15 minutes to earn one Singapore dollar (£0.59), with only one logged session allowed per day. But behavioural scientists and psychologists told the Guardian such a scheme could still help boost a habit in precipitous decline. Continue reading...

data.title: Anthony Page obituary
data.description: Stage and screen director behind landmark productions of Samuel Beckett, John Osborne and Edward Albee Anthony Page, who has died aged 90, was one of a group of talented and individual – sometimes wilful – directors who helped establish the English Stage Company at the Royal Court in London at the end of the 1950s and the early 60s. The company, led by George Devine and Tony Richardson, became the seedbed of modern playwriting, notably John Osborne ’s Look Back in Anger (1956) in a repertoire that embraced Beckett, Brecht, Ionesco, Arthur Miller and Tennessee Williams, as well as the native voices of Arnold Wesker , Ann Jellicoe , John Arden and NF Simpson . data.title: Tim Dowling: could the new dog’s tricks make her into a star?
data.description: Two women I meet on our walk are way more interested in Jean than me – and insist she’ll clean up if we enter her in the local dog show It’s a Saturday morning and I’m walking the dog on a vast bit of scrubland. The path in front of me is parched and deserted. Up ahead, the dog turns the corner at a patch of brambles, and I hear the excited voices of two women. My immediate reaction is one of alarm; I whistle, but the dog doesn’t reappear. The voices rise. Only when I turn the corner myself do I see that everything is fine: the dog is dashing from one woman to the other, tail wagging, and the women are both delighted. Meanwhile, their own dogs stand to one side, staring balefully at the ground, leads trailing. Continue reading...

data.title: Henry Harris’ recipe for tomatoes, creme fraiche and herbs
data.description: Sumptuous, late-summer tomatoes cooked with cream and served on toast? Supper is served in 10 … OK, maybe 15 minutes Forty years ago, an antiquarian bookseller recommended to me Edouard de Pomiane’s La cuisine en dix minutes , a selection of recipes that could be cooked at home in less than 10 minutes. A scientist and food lover, de Pomiane stripped back what was then viewed as a very complicated craft, and also gave the time-poor an opportunity to cook and enjoy a good meal made from good ingredients. This was the first recipe I cooked from that book, and it is still a great favourite that has punctuated my menus ever since. Henry Harris is chef/co-owner of Bouchon Racine , London EC1. His book, The Racine Effect, is published by Quadrille at £40. To order a copy for £36, go to guardianbookshop.com Continue reading...

data.title: Talk less, listen more and six other top tips on giving good advice
data.description: Are you someone who thinks they have all the answers? Is your experience relevant here? Experts on the questions to ask yourself before giving advice “Often, when people approach you for advice, they just want to talk about how they feel,” says Annalisa Barbieri, advice columnist for the Guardian for almost 20 years. For example, you might vent to a friend about your awful boss, and if they’re shocked it could confirm you’re being treated badly. “I also think people can have a lot of shame when things aren’t working out, and we like to share shame because it’s a hot potato of a feeling.” In other words, not every situation warrants advice. Sometimes, the person just wants to gauge a reaction or to share. Continue reading...

data.title: A Swedish company is transforming discarded wind turbines into tiny-solar powered homes and recycled skis
data.description: The challenge of decommissioned wind turbine blades is becoming increasingly prominent in Europe. In response, various companies are working on inventive reuse projects that could transform these retired assets into valuable materials, underscoring the necessity for a regulatory structure that supports sustainable initiatives in this industry.

data.title: Fourteen tail vertebrae found in Spain replaces North America as the only Diplodocus site
data.description: A significant paleontological breakthrough has occurred in Spain, where researchers have identified the first confirmed Diplodocus fossils beyond North America. The discovery implies that during the Late Jurassic era, declining sea levels could have permitted dinosaurs to migrate between continents.

data.title: Ending the nuclear arms race starts with cities doing their part
data.description:
The catastrophic danger posed to cities by nuclear weapons is nothing new. Putting major urban areas at risk across generations is, in fact, the point of these weapons of terror. The practice of doing so is benignly called nuclear deterrence, but it requires holding the cities of adversaries – real and imagined – under constant threat.
The use of even the smallest nuclear weapons in today’s arsenals would cause a humanitarian emergency in cities. That is why city leadership should have a voice...

data.title: Na Terra Indígena Jaraguá, o futebol transcende a dimensão esportiva
data.description: O futebol brasileiro sempre foi gigante. Gigante antes das bets, gigante apesar delas. Não é possível aceitar que o futebol dependa de um sistema de financiamento sustentado pelo vício em jogos e por tudo de ruim que ele causa às famílias. O futebol é para salvar, não para acabar com a vida de ninguém. Leia mais (09/18/2026 - 20h12)

data.translatedTitle: Diana's brother stands by his words about Charles
data.translatedDescription: The war of words between Earl Spencer - brother of Princess Diana - and King Charles escalates. The earl stands by his harsh criticism of Charles' behavior in the wake of Diana's death. - I am telling the truth.

data.title: Sophia spontanköpte en åsna på festresan: ”Toppar nog allt”
data.description: Tjejresa, bröllop, fest och drinkar. Och så en åsna på det. – När vi är ute och festar med tjejerna så brukar det bli lite bus och rave. Men det här toppar nog allt faktiskt, säger Sophia Olsson Jacobsen.
data.translatedTitle: Sophia spontaneously bought a donkey on the party trip: "Probably tops everything"
data.translatedDescription: Girls trip, wedding, party and drinks. And then a donkey at that. - When we're out partying with the girls, there's usually a bit of mischief and a rave. But this probably tops everything, says Sophia Olsson Jacobsen.

data.title: Ledare: Någon måste vara konstruktiv, bara inte jag – sa Ulf Kristersson
data.description: Ulf Kristersson har förlorat, kan se att läget är låst, men är ändå avspänd. Han tänker inte ta ansvar.
data.translatedTitle: Leader: Someone has to be constructive, just not me - said Ulf Kristersson
data.translatedDescription: Ulf Kristersson has lost, can see that the situation is locked, but is still relaxed. He is not going to take responsibility.

data.title: Så ska landslaget få fart på Viktor Gyökeres
data.description: Han var den viktigaste spelaren när Sverige tog sig till fotbolls-VM. Men den nya har säsongen börjat tungt för Viktor Gyökeres. Nu hoppas landslaget kunna putsa upp anfallarens forna stjärnglans. – Det finns inga problem ur vår synvinkel. Vi älskar Viktor, säger förbundskaptenen Graham Potter.
data.translatedTitle: This is how the national team will get Viktor Gyökeres up to speed
data.translatedDescription: He was the most important player when Sweden made it to the World Cup. But the new season has started heavily for Viktor Gyökeres. Now the national team hopes to polish up the striker's former star shine. - There are no problems from our point of view. We love Viktor, says national team captain Graham Potter.

data.title: Johan Croneman: Bara en viktig sak skiljer Graham Potter från tidigare förbundskaptener
data.description: När fotbollsherrarnas förbundskapten Graham Potter pratar detaljerat om till exempel betydelsen av en särskilt vänsterfot ger det en känsla av hans noggrannhet och helhetssyn, det skriver DN:s sport-i-tv-krönikör Johan Croneman i veckans krönika.
data.translatedTitle: Johan Croneman: Only one important thing separates Graham Potter from former national team captains
data.translatedDescription: When men's football captain Graham Potter talks in detail about, for example, the importance of a particular left foot, it gives a sense of his accuracy and holistic view, writes DN's sports-i-tv columnist Johan Croneman in this week's column.

data.title: Experter: Så pratar du med barnen efter överfallsvåldtäkten
data.description: Efter den misstänkta överfallsvåldtäkten mot ett barn i Järfälla är många föräldrar oroliga. Behåll lugnet, prata med ditt barn och ljug inte – det är några av experternas råd.
data.translatedTitle: Experts: How to talk to children after assault rape
data.translatedDescription: After the suspected rape of a child in Järfälla, many parents are worried. Keep calm, talk to your child and don't lie - that's some of the advice from the experts.

data.title: Ståhlis: Ja, vad gör han egentligen på jobbet hela dagarna?
data.description: Ståhlis hamnar i ett väntrum och tjuvlyssnar på en uppfriskande medpatient. Men hallå Douglas, var kissar du egentligen?
data.translatedTitle: Ståhlis: Yes, what does he actually do at work all day?
data.translatedDescription: Ståhlis ends up in a waiting room and eavesdrops on a refreshing fellow patient. But hey Douglas, where do you really pee?

data.title: Så ökar agenternas inflytande i bokbranschen
data.description: Nästa vecka öppnar Bokmässan i Göteborg. I år tar agenterna större plats än någonsin. Riskerar deras ökande inflytande att göra litteraturen strömlinjeformad? Eller är det ett sätt att ge mer makt åt författarna? – Det är svårt att bli riktigt kommersiellt framgångsrik författare utan en agent, säger forskaren Karl Berglund.
data.translatedTitle: This increases the influence of agents in the book industry
data.translatedDescription: Next week the Book Fair opens in Gothenburg. This year, the agents take up more space than ever. Does their increasing influence risk streamlining the literature? Or is it a way to give more power to the authors? - It is difficult to become a truly commercially successful author without an agent, says researcher Karl Berglund.

data.title: ”Jimmie Åkesson väckte den björn som sov”
data.description: ÖREBRO. Gå och rösta. Så löd uppmaningen från Örebro moské när valrörelsen kantades av antimuslimska utspel. Samtidigt knackade vänsterpartister som Nadja Awad på tusentals dörrar och lovade frysta hyror. Soffliggare strömmade till V i Sveriges utsatta områden. – Jimmie Åkesson väckte den björn som sov, säger Vivallabon Yonis Abokor.
data.translatedTitle: "Jimmie Åkesson woke the sleeping bear"
data.translatedDescription: ÖREBRIDGE. Go and vote. This was the call from the Örebro mosque when the election campaign was marred by anti-Muslim outbursts. Meanwhile, leftists like Nadja Awad knocked on thousands of doors, promising frozen rents. Couch sleepers flocked to V in Sweden's vulnerable areas. - Jimmie Åkesson woke up the sleeping bear, says Vivallabon Yonis Abokor.

data.title: Catia Hultquist: Det ska fan vara ung och gravid under ozempic-eran
data.description: Den smalhetsande samtiden tycks inte väja ens för graviditeter. I alla fall verkar det så när man ser H&M:s nya bilder med klädreklam för gravida och ammande, det skriver DN:s Catia Hultquist.
data.translatedTitle: Catia Hultquist: It must be young and pregnant during the ozempic era
data.translatedDescription: The thinness of the present does not seem to be favorable even for pregnancies. In any case, it seems so when you see H&M's new pictures with clothing advertising for pregnant and breastfeeding women, writes DN's Catia Hultquist.

data.title: Acne-grundaren Jonny Johansson: ”Det är bra att våra jeans är dyra”
data.description: Han drömde om att bli rockstjärna – i stället blev han klädskaparen som i tre decennier har fått modeälskare världen över att sukta efter mer. Jonny Johansson, Acne Studios grundare och kreativa chef, förklarar hur mode ska spegla världen och varför ett par jeans kan – ska! – kosta 15 000 kronor.
data.translatedTitle: Acne founder Jonny Johansson: "It's good that our jeans are expensive"
data.translatedDescription: He dreamed of being a rock star — instead, he became the designer of clothes that for three decades has left fashion lovers around the world yearning for more. Jonny Johansson, Acne Studio's founder and creative director, explains how fashion should reflect the world and why a pair of jeans can - should! - cost SEK 15,000.

data.title: Hösten är bästa tiden att samlas kring grillen
data.description: Att samlas kring grillen är särskilt härligt på hösten, och glöden värmer både mat och människor. Jens Linder lyfter matlagningen med säsongens råvaror. Recept: Jens Linder Foto: Daniel Costantini
data.translatedTitle: Autumn is the best time to gather around the barbecue
data.translatedDescription: Gathering around the grill is especially lovely in autumn, and the glow warms both food and people. Jens Linder elevates cooking with seasonal ingredients. Recipe: Jens Linder Photo: Daniel Costantini

data.title: Jens Linder: Matlagning som glödande protest mot mörkret
data.description: Krönika. Att grilla på hösten är inte bara värmande och gott. Det är också en glödande protest mot Nordens mörker och kyla, tycker Jens Linder.
data.translatedTitle: Jens Linder: Cooking as a glowing protest against the dark
data.translatedDescription: Chronicle. Grilling in autumn is not only warming and tasty. It is also a glowing protest against the darkness and cold of the Nordics, thinks Jens Linder.

data.title: 10 saker att inte glömma i höstträdgården: ”Många missar vitlökståget”
data.description: Många ser våren som startskottet för trädgårdsarbetet. Men den som fortsätter påta på hösten har mycket att vinna nästa säsong: tid, pengar, ett mer klimatsmart odlande – och en större, tidigare skörd. Här är experternas 10 bästa hösthacks.
data.translatedTitle: 10 things not to forget in the autumn garden: "Many miss the garlic train"
data.translatedDescription: Many see spring as the starting point for gardening. But those who continue planting in autumn have a lot to gain next season: time, money, more climate-smart cultivation - and a larger, earlier harvest. Here are the experts' top 10 fall hacks.

data.title: Amanda Sokolnicki: Tidöhögern har förlorat valet – och skyller på väljarna
data.description: Det Tidöpartierna har visat efter förlusten är inte vackert. När slutade man betrakta invandrare som legitima väljare?
data.translatedTitle: Amanda Sokolnicki: Tidöhöger has lost the election - and blames the voters
data.translatedDescription: What the Tidö parties have shown after the loss is not pretty. When did immigrants stop being considered legitimate voters?

data.title: Insändare. Rusta sjukvården samtidigt som försvaret
data.description: INSÄNDARE. Bara tre av landets 21 regioner skulle klara av att ta emot många skadade vid en krigssituation eller terrorattack.
data.translatedTitle: Letter to the editor. Equip healthcare at the same time as defence
data.translatedDescription: LETTER TO THE EDITOR. Only three of the country's 21 regions would be able to receive many casualties in a war situation or terrorist attack.

data.title: Danmark och USA tecknar Grönlandsavtal
data.description: Danmark och USA har nått ett avtal om säkerheten på Grönland, uppger president Donald Trump. Enligt den danska statsministerns kansli väntas avtalet undertecknas nästa vecka. ”Avtalet erkänner kungarikets suveränitet och territoriella integritet samt det grönländska folkets rätt till självbestämmande”, säger Mette Frederiksen i ett pressmeddelande.
data.translatedTitle: Denmark and the USA sign the Greenland Agreement
data.translatedDescription: Denmark and the United States have reached an agreement on the security of Greenland, says President Donald Trump. According to the Danish Prime Minister's office, the agreement is expected to be signed next week. "The agreement recognizes the kingdom's sovereignty and territorial integrity as well as the Greenlandic people's right to self-determination," says Mette Frederiksen in a press release.

data.title: Karl Dalén: Beskedet visar hur pressad Trump känner sig
data.description: WASHINGTON. Donald Trumps beslut att porta flera stora mediebolag från Vita huset var oväntat – men ändå inte. Sedan han tillträdde har presidenten försökt påverka journalistiken på en rad olika sätt. Nu tar han till storsläggan – i en tid när opinionssiffrorna är rekordlåga.
data.translatedTitle: Karl Dalén: The message shows how pressured Trump feels
data.translatedDescription: WASHINGTON. Donald Trump's decision to port several major media companies from the White House was unexpected - but still not. Since taking office, the president has tried to influence journalism in a number of different ways. Now he takes the big sledgehammer – at a time when public opinion figures are at record lows.

data.title: Ungern lättar på Orbáns hbtq-lagar
data.description: I juni presenterade Ungerns nya premiärminister Péter Magyar det han kallar ”Operation renande eld” – avvecklingen av Viktor Orbáns ”maffiapolitik”. Bland annat har han luckrat upp delar av den stränga lagstiftning riktad mot hbtq-personer som Orbán införde. Ett steg på vägen, men långt i från tillräckligt, menar Human Rights Watch.
data.translatedTitle: Hungary eases Orbán's LGBT laws
data.translatedDescription: In June, Hungary's new Prime Minister Péter Magyar presented what he calls "Operation Cleansing Fire" - the dismantling of Viktor Orbán's "mafia politics". Among other things, he has loosened parts of the strict legislation aimed at LGBTQ people that Orbán introduced. A step along the way, but far from enough, says Human Rights Watch.

data.title: Modo pajade rekordfesten i Stockholm
data.description: Fullsatt och nytt premiärrekord i Avicii arena. Men hemmalaget AIK fick inte festa med hemmasupportrarna. Modo kontrollerade hem det tänkta toppmötet med 3–1.
data.translatedTitle: Modo rocked the record party in Stockholm
data.translatedDescription: Full and new premiere record in Avicii arena. But the home team AIK did not get to party with the home supporters. Modo controlled home the intended summit with 3–1.

data.title: Trump portar flera medier från Vita huset: ”Lögner”
data.description: Donald Trump portar flera stora medier från Vita huset med omedelbar verkan. Presidenten anklagar CNN, Politico och MS NOW för att sprida falska uppgifter. CNN står helt bakom teamet i Vita huset och deras rapportering, säger mediebolaget i ett uttalande.
data.translatedTitle: Trump brings several media from the White House: "Lies"
data.translatedDescription: Donald Trump is removing several major media outlets from the White House with immediate effect. The president accuses CNN, Politico and MS NOW of spreading false information. CNN stands fully behind the White House team and their reporting, the media company said in a statement.

data.title: Säkerhetsexpert larmar om USA-kopplad husaffär på Grönland
data.description: Ett amerikanskt investmentbolag betalade miljonbelopp till den grönländska toppolitikern Vivian Motzfeldts sambo för ett hus i Nuuk. Nu väcker affären nya frågor om politiskt inflytande och amerikanska intressen på Grönland. – De vill utan tvekan ha något tillbaka, säger säkerhetsexperten Marc Jacobsen till TV2.
data.translatedTitle: Security expert warns about US-linked house deal in Greenland
data.translatedDescription: An American investment company paid millions to the partner of Greenland's top politician Vivian Motzfeldt for a house in Nuuk. Now the affair raises new questions about political influence and American interests in Greenland. - They undoubtedly want something back, says security expert Marc Jacobsen to TV2.

data.title: 18 september: Missa inte dagens nyheter
data.description: Andersson får sondera, bibeln förnyas och nytt kattdjur – här är dagens nyheter.
data.translatedTitle: 18 september: Missa inte dagens nyheter
data.translatedDescription: Andersson gets to probe, the Bible is renewed and a new cat - here are today's news.

data.title: Hamilton Steiner: ”Operation Vivaldi” gör Putins första mål alltmer avlägset
data.description: KIEV. ”Operation Vivaldi” kan vara Ukrainas största framgång vid fronten i år. Även om den inte kastar om spelplanen i kriget har motoffensiven stort symboliskt värde – Kremls önskedröm om att kontrollera hela Donbass är nu ännu mer avlägsen.
data.translatedTitle: Hamilton Steiner: ”Operation Vivaldi” gör Putins första mål alltmer avlägset
data.translatedDescription: KIEV. "Operation Vivaldi" may be Ukraine's biggest success at the front this year. Although it does not change the playing field in the war, the counter-offensive has great symbolic value – the Kremlin's wishful dream of controlling all of Donbass is now even more distant.

data.title: Kristofer Ahlström: Elon Musks ”The odyssey”-film är ett rejält haveri
data.description: Elon Musk utlovade en miljon kronor för en ”historiskt korrekt” AI-version av Christopher Nolans storfilm. Resultatet lämnar en del övrigt att önska – däribland historisk korrekthet, skriver DN:s Kristofer Ahlström.
data.translatedTitle: Kristofer Ahlström: Elon Musks ”The odyssey”-film är ett rejält haveri
data.translatedDescription: Elon Musk promised one million kroner for a "historically accurate" AI version of Christopher Nolan's blockbuster. The result leaves something to be desired - including historical accuracy, writes DN's Kristofer Ahlström.

data.title: Max Hjelm: Mobbat, straffat och hotat – Kanadas motdrag är välkommet
data.description: I flera europeiska länder är nationalister farligt nära makten, och drömmer om att göra vår kära union mer sluten. De stärkta vänskaperna mellan EU och Kanada visar att det finns en annan väg.
data.translatedTitle: Max Hjelm: Mobbat, straffat och hotat – Kanadas motdrag är välkommet
data.translatedDescription: In several European countries, nationalists are dangerously close to power, and dream of making our dear union more closed. The strengthened friendships between the EU and Canada show that there is another way.

data.title: DN Debatt. ”Här är vad de egentligen menar när de talar om ’röstboskap’”
data.description: DN DEBATT. Just nu pågår en debatt om huruvida muslimska röster tippade över valresultatet till vänstersidans fördel. När människor med utländsk bakgrund inte röstar är de ett tecken på misslyckad integration, men när de inte röstar precis som ni vill utmålas de plötsligt som ett hot. Hur ska ni ha det? skriver fem forskare vid Handelshögskolan i Stockholm.
data.translatedTitle: DN Debatt. ”Här är vad de egentligen menar när de talar om ’röstboskap’”
data.translatedDescription: DN DEBATE. Right now there is a debate about whether Muslim votes tipped the election result in favor of the left. When people with a foreign background don't vote, they are a sign of failed integration, but when they don't vote exactly the way you want them to, they are suddenly portrayed as a threat. How are you going? write five researchers at the Stockholm School of Economics.

data.title: Mustaschkupp och skolstrid – nu är kommunen SD:s starkaste fäste
data.description: Färgelanda är Sverigedemokraternas starkaste fäste i landet. Med 39 procent av rösterna har partiet tagit hem en jordskredsseger i kommunalvalet. Bakom resultatet finns en skolkonflikt, flera år av röda siffror och en uppmärksammad Jimmie-mustasch.
data.translatedTitle: Mustaschkupp och skolstrid – nu är kommunen SD:s starkaste fäste
data.translatedDescription: Färgelanda is the Sweden Democrats' strongest stronghold in the country. With 39 percent of the vote, the party has won a landslide victory in the municipal election. Behind the result is a school conflict, several years of red numbers and a noticeable Jimmie mustache.

data.title: Chantal Akermans mor-dotter-bok är förkrossande vacker
data.description: Regissören Chantal Akerman har gjort ”världens bästa film genom tiderna”. Men hon har också skrivit en både becksvart och livsbejakande roman som nu finns på svenska – en stor kulturgärning, jublar Jan Holmberg.
data.translatedTitle: Chantal Akermans mor-dotter-bok är förkrossande vacker
data.translatedDescription: Director Chantal Akerman has made "the world's best film of all time". But she has also written a pitch-black and life-affirming novel that is now available in Swedish - a great cultural achievement, exults Jan Holmberg.

data.title: Kvinna försökte döda sin make med D-vitamin – döms
data.description: Under flera års tid smög kvinnan ner D-vitamin i makens vattenflaska och hans chilisås. Syftet var att långsamt men metodiskt förgifta mannen och döda honom. Nu döms hon till tolv års fängelse för mordförsök.
data.translatedTitle: Kvinna försökte döda sin make med D-vitamin – döms
data.translatedDescription: For several years, the woman slipped vitamin D into her husband's water bottle and his chili sauce. The aim was to slowly but methodically poison the man and kill him. Now she is sentenced to twelve years in prison for attempted murder.

data.title: Johan Nilsson: En desperat jakt på alternativ till antibiotika
data.description: Antibiotika fungerar allt sämre – och snart kanske inte alls. Inför ett sådant skräckscenario pågår jakten på alternativ. Om försöken med bakteriofager lyckas återstå att se. Oavsett är forskarna värda all respekt.
data.translatedTitle: Johan Nilsson: En desperat jakt på alternativ till antibiotika
data.translatedDescription: Antibiotics work less and less – and soon may not work at all. In the face of such a horror scenario, the search for alternatives is ongoing. Whether the experiments with bacteriophages are successful remains to be seen. Regardless, the researchers deserve all respect.

data.title: Här framställs virus som ska ”äta” resistenta bakterier
data.description: LYON. Ett slags virus som ”äter” bakterier kan bli ett nytt vapen mot antibiotikaresistens. Frankrike satsar stort på produktion av så kallade bakteriofager. – Alla europeiska sjukhus borde ha tillgång till detta, på samma sätt som man har blodbanker, säger Frédéric Laurent vid Universitetssjukhuset i Lyon. Men är metoden säker?
data.translatedTitle: Här framställs virus som ska ”äta” resistenta bakterier
data.translatedDescription: LYON. A kind of virus that "eats" bacteria could become a new weapon against antibiotic resistance. France invests heavily in the production of so-called bacteriophages. - All European hospitals should have access to this, in the same way as you have blood banks, says Frédéric Laurent at the University Hospital in Lyon. But is the method safe?

data.title: Tove Lo: ”Att skaffa barn är the final boss av äventyr”
data.description: Uppkäftiga, explicita och ofta smutsiga textrader har gjort Tove Lo till en världsartist. Den känslan kommer från kroppen, medan min hjärna säger blankt ”nej”, säger Tove Lo till DN.

data.title: Insändare. Politik borde vara det möjligas konst även nu
data.description: INSÄNDARE. I de flesta sakpolitikiska frågor bör Centerpartiet och Vänsterpartiet kunna komma överens. Men det förutsätter att man släpper på prestigen och öppnar för att ta till sig fakta från forskarvärlden, skriver den tidigare forskaren Eva Asplund.
data.translatedTitle: Letter to the editor. Politics should be the art of the possible even now
data.translatedDescription: LETTER TO THE EDITOR. In most substantive and political issues, the Center Party and the Left Party should be able to agree. But that presupposes that one lets go of prestige and opens up to absorbing facts from the scientific world, writes former researcher Eva Asplund.

data.title: Miley Cyrus nya skiva är som en småseg tisdag i radiohitfabriken
data.description: Världsstjärnan Miley Cyrus ambition och musikaliska skicklighet förvaltas inte riktigt på nya albumet ”Bass persuades”. Det finns förtjänster, men helheten blir lite för tråkig och slätstruken, skriver DN:s Gabriel Zetterström.
data.translatedTitle: Miley Cyrus' new album is like a slow Tuesday in the radio hit factory
data.translatedDescription: World star Miley Cyrus's ambition and musical skill are not really managed on the new album "Bass persuades". There are merits, but the whole becomes a bit too boring and flat, writes DN's Gabriel Zetterström.

data.title: DN väljer: Här är veckans bästa låtar, vecka 38

data.title: Sidan om gonorré mest besökt: ”Oroväckande”
data.description: I augusti toppade könssjukdomen gonorré listan över mest besökta sidor på 1177 i region Stockholm. Flera orsaker kan ligga bakom siffran. – Man funderar kanske på vad man har gjort under sommaren, säger sexualupplysaren Pelle Ullholm.
data.translatedTitle: Gonorrhea page most visited: "Worrying"
data.translatedDescription: In August, the venereal disease gonorrhea topped the list of most visited pages at 1177 in the Stockholm region. Several reasons can lie behind the figure. - You might think about what you have done during the summer, says sex informant Pelle Ullholm.

data.title: Man häktad för grov våldtäkt mot barn i Järfälla
data.description: En man har under fredagen häktats misstänkt för grov våldtäkt mot barn i Järfälla. Tidigare i veckan begärdes en annan person häktad för brottet – men begäran drogs senare tillbaka. Kommunen uppmanar även fortsatt föräldrar att följa sina barn till och från skolan.
data.translatedTitle: Man detained for aggravated rape of children in Järfälla
data.translatedDescription: A man was arrested on Friday on suspicion of aggravated rape against a child in Järfälla. Earlier this week, another person was requested to be detained for the crime - but the request was later withdrawn. The municipality also continues to urge parents to accompany their children to and from school.

data.title: Håkan Nessers hämndorgie lyfter först mot slutet av nya romanen
data.description: ”Domino” hade kunnat bli en av Håkan Nessers bästa romaner om inte hans hämndlystnad kommit i vägen, skriver Kerstin Särneö.
data.translatedTitle: Håkan Nesser's revenge orgy only takes off towards the end of the new novel
data.translatedDescription: "Domino" could have become one of Håkan Nesser's best novels if his desire for revenge had not gotten in the way, writes Kerstin Särneö.

data.title: Supersopranen Lise Davidsen glänser på månadens klassiska skiva
data.description: Den norska supersopranen Lise Davidsen är kapabel att vigt skifta mellan lyriskt skimmer och maffigt tryck. På nya albumet ”Verdi” kommer hennes skills till sin fulla rätt, skriver DN:s Camilla Lundberg om månadens klassiska.
data.translatedTitle: The super-soprano Lise Davidsen shines on this month's classical record
data.translatedDescription: The Norwegian super-soprano Lise Davidsen is capable of shifting between lyrical shimmer and mammoth pressure. On the new album "Verdi", her skills come to their full potential, writes DN's Camilla Lundberg about this month's classic.

data.title: Talmansrundorna är inledda – fortsatt låst mellan C och V
data.description: Vänsterpartiet kräver att få ingå i en regering medan Centerpartiet insisterar på att de ska hållas utanför. Positionerna på oppositionens sida verkar fortsatt låsta efter att talmansrundorna inletts på fredagen. – V har ju varit väldigt tydliga med att de inte vill ha ett organiserat samarbete på något sätt, säger Centerledaren till DN.
data.translatedTitle: Speaker rounds have begun - still locked between C and V
data.translatedDescription: The Left Party demands to be included in a government, while the Center Party insists that they should be kept out. The positions on the opposition side still seem locked after the speaker rounds began on Friday. - V has been very clear that they do not want an organized collaboration in any way, says the Center leader to DN.

data.title: Andrew Scott lyfter tryckande krigsdrama om förspelet till D-dagen
data.description: I ”Pressure” blir väderprognosen en krigsavgörande fråga när Andrew Scott spelar meteorologen som vågade trotsa militärens önsketänkande inför D-Dagen. Det är ett välskräddat men stundtals segdraget drama, lyft av Scotts intensivt återhållna närvaro, tycker Fredrik Sahlin.
data.translatedTitle: Andrew Scott lifts poignant war drama about the run-up to D-Day
data.translatedDescription: In "Pressure", the weather forecast becomes a decisive issue in war when Andrew Scott plays the meteorologist who dared to defy the military's wishful thinking before D-Day. It is a well-tailored but sometimes tenacious drama, lifted by Scott's intensely restrained presence, Fredrik Sahlin thinks.

data.title: Läckert och avskalat när Barbara Hannigan intar Berwaldhallen

data.translatedTitle: Delicious and stripped down when Barbara Hannigan occupies Berwaldhallen
data.translatedDescription: In the Berwaldhallen, Barbara Hannigan, together with the conductor George Benjamin and the pianist Bertrand Chamoyou, moves between the clear and the musty. DN's Camilla Lundberg experiences a concert of kaleidoscopic richness of color and tickling sounds.

data.title: Småpartier på högersidan större än blockskillnaden
data.description: SD-företrädare har sedan riksdagsvalet vid flera tillfällen riktat kritik mot väljare som lagt sina röster på partier utanför riksdagen. Med knappt 1 500 distrikt kvar att räkna i den slutliga rösträkningen står klart att Örebropartiet och Alternativ för Sverige tillsammans fått drygt 52 000 röster, mer än de drygt 50 000 röster som skiljer blocken emellan.
data.translatedTitle: Small lots on the right side larger than the block difference
data.translatedDescription: Since the Riksdag election, SD representatives have on several occasions directed criticism at voters who cast their votes for parties outside the Riksdag. With barely 1,500 districts left to count in the final vote count, it is clear that the Örebro Party and Alternativ för Sverige together received just over 52,000 votes, more than the roughly 50,000 votes that separate the blocs.

data.title: Klart: Lågpriskedjan flyttar in på lyxvaruhuset NK
data.description: Efter en tid av obekräftade rykten står det nu klart – lågpriskedjan Lidl flyttar in på anrika lyxvaruhuset NK i Stockholm. – För oss handlar det om att göra NK ännu mer relevant i människors vardag och ge våra kunder ytterligare en anledning att besöka varuhuset, säger Hannes Hasselrot, vd för Nordiska Kompaniet i ett uttalande.
data.translatedTitle: Clear: The discount chain is moving into the luxury department store NK
data.translatedDescription: After a period of unconfirmed rumours, it is now clear - the discount chain Lidl is moving into the long-established luxury department store NK in Stockholm. - For us, it's about making NK even more relevant in people's everyday lives and giving our customers another reason to visit the department store, says Hannes Hasselrot, CEO of Nordiska Kompaniet in a statement.

data.title: De Duitse industrie verliest vele tienduizenden banen door de China-schok. ‘Deze Chinese pomp kost de helft van een Duitse’
data.description: In industrieland Duitsland groeit het onbehagen over de moordende concurrentie uit China. De roep om invoerheffingen zwelt aan. Ook machinebouwer Aura in Rijnland-Palts voelt de druk van de Chinezen. Is er toekomst voor Made in Germany ?
data.translatedTitle: German industry is losing tens of thousands of jobs due to the China shock. 'This Chinese pump costs half of a German one'
data.translatedDescription: In industrialized Germany, there is growing unease about the cutthroat competition from China. The call for import taxes is growing. Machine builder Aura in Rhineland-Palatinate is also feeling the pressure from the Chinese. Is there a future for Made in Germany?

data.title: Het was voor zijn ‘familie en toekomstige kinderen’ dat Rini H. een tafelblad en een putdeksel naar de politie gooide
data.description: Wat bewoog de mensen die een jaar geleden bij rechts-extremistische rellen brand stichtten en in gevecht gingen met de politie? In de rechtszaal noemt de een zorgen om de toekomst van Nederland, een ander de woningnood. Weer anderen wijten het aan persoonlijke sores en de „wodka en benzo’s”.
data.translatedTitle: It was for his 'family and future children' that Rini H. threw a table top and a manhole cover at the police
data.translatedDescription: What motivated the people who set fires and fought with the police during right-wing extremist riots a year ago? In the courtroom, one person mentions concerns about the future of the Netherlands, another the housing shortage. Still others blame it on personal troubles and “vodka and benzos.”

data.title: Discriminatie door de politie? ‘Witte Nederlanders hebben geen idee wat we meemaken’
data.description: In Zuidwijk, de Rotterdamse buurt waar vorige week een 51-jarige man overleed bij een hardhandige arrestatie, overheerst het gevoel dat er sprake was van discriminatie. „Iedereen van kleur heeft verhalen over confrontaties met de politie.”
data.translatedTitle: Discrimination by the police? 'White Dutch people have no idea what we are experiencing'
data.translatedDescription: In Zuidwijk, the Rotterdam neighborhood where a 51-year-old man died last week in a heavy-handed arrest, there is a prevailing feeling that there was discrimination. “Everyone of color has stories about confrontations with the police.”

data.title: Waar komen al die burn-outs vandaan? ‘Het heet werk-privébalans, ik noem het werk-privékeuzes’
data.description: Werknemers vallen vaker en langer uit – vooral vrouwen tussen de 31 en 40 jaar. De oorzaken zijn divers: thuiswerken, meer prikkels, de combinatie van zorg en werk. Werkgevers kunnen niet overal wat aan doen. „Jongeren vergelijken zich meer met anderen.”
data.translatedTitle: Where do all those burnouts come from? 'It's called work-life balance, I call it work-life choices'
data.translatedDescription: Employees drop out more often and for longer - especially women between the ages of 31 and 40. The causes are diverse: working from home, more incentives, the combination of care and work. Employers cannot do something about everything. “Young people compare themselves more with others.”

data.title: AI-topmannen voorspellen doem. Is AI echt een existentieel gevaar?
data.description: AI-bedrijven waarschuwen voor extreme risico’s, maar onder veiligheidsexperts is grote verdeeldheid over hoe reëel het gevaar is. En tussen een AI-hack en uitroeiing zitten nogal wat stappen. Toch: „Menselijk uitsterven is nogal een dingetje.”
data.translatedTitle: AI executives predict doom. Is AI really an existential danger?
data.translatedDescription: AI companies warn of extreme risks, but there is great disagreement among security experts about how real the danger is. And there are quite a few steps between an AI hack and eradication. Still: “Human extinction is quite a big deal.”

data.title: ‘Daden van terreur’ of schouderophalen over ‘rare dingen’
data.description: Sabotage-acties legden dinsdag het treinverkeer in Oost-Nederland plat, maar dat leidde vooral tot onderkoelde reacties. „De terloopsheid waarmee dit gaat en wordt geaccepteerd, vind ik verontrustend.”
data.translatedTitle: “Acts of terror” or shrugging at “weird things”
data.translatedDescription: Sabotage actions paralyzed train traffic in the eastern Netherlands on Tuesday, but this mainly led to subdued reactions. “I find the casualness with which this is done and accepted disturbing.”

data.translatedDescription: The Netherlands is making 12 million euros available for medical aid to Palestinian children. Before the summer, a majority of the House of Representatives called on the cabinet to come up with a concrete plan.

data.title: In de week nadat de wereld werd gewaarschuwd voor een catastrofe, is de spanning in AI-hoofdstad San Francisco voelbaar

data.translatedTitle: The far-right bloc is large, but its political effectiveness remains small
data.translatedDescription: Joost Eerdmans (JA21) was in a position this week at the General Political Considerations to make many demands on the minority cabinet. But he made a strategic mistake. Typical of the limited political influence of the right flank.

data.translatedDescription: The government's policy of building very quickly and in large numbers of affordable homes is working against itself on some points. Researchers calculated the consequences.

data.title: ‘De kinderen vonden het leuk om even met iets anders bezig te zijn’
data.description: Het laatste dat fotograaf Lisa van den Berg (25) wilde, is dat de kinderen op haar foto’s er zielig uit zouden zien. Ze zijn wel ziek, net zoals zij was als kind. „In het ziekenhuis gaat het veel over jou, bijna niemand praat met jou. Ik deed dat wel, ik kwam voor hen.”
data.translatedTitle: 'The children enjoyed doing something different for a while'
data.translatedDescription: The last thing photographer Lisa van den Berg (25) wanted was for the children in her photos to look pitiful. They are sick, just like she was as a child. “In the hospital it is a lot about you, hardly anyone talks to you. I did, I came for them.”

data.translatedDescription: To break away from the US, Canada and Europe are flirting with each other. But while Carney takes flight, the EU continues to hesitate.

data.title: Ik eer een oom die 84 jaar dood is, en dat heeft zin
data.description: Wat is er gebeurd met haar oom Herman, die in de Tweede Wereldoorlog gestorven is? Rosan Hollak schreef een boek over het onverwerkte verdriet van haar moeder en ontdekte wat het betekent om een jongen, die uit de geschiedenis werd gewist, weer een gezicht te geven.
data.translatedTitle: I honor an uncle who has been dead 84 years, and that makes sense
data.translatedDescription: What happened to her uncle Herman, who died in the Second World War? Rosan Hollak wrote a book about her mother's unresolved grief and discovered what it means to give a face to a boy who was erased from history.

data.title: Zanger Harry van der Kamp (1947-2026) wilde de klank van de Renaissance vereeuwigen
data.description: Harry van der Kamp had een hypnotiserende basstem, waarmee hij onder anderen Nederlands grootste componist Jan Pieterszoon Sweelinck uit de vergetelheid zong. „Een gedreven kunstenaar met een zachtaardig en poëtisch hart.”
data.translatedTitle: Singer Harry van der Kamp (1947-2026) wanted to immortalize the sound of the Renaissance
data.translatedDescription: Harry van der Kamp had a hypnotic bass voice, with which he, among others, sang the Netherlands' greatest composer Jan Pieterszoon Sweelinck from oblivion. “A passionate artist with a gentle and poetic heart.”

data.title: Suzanna Jansen: ‘Ik heb altijd een grote verantwoordelijkheid gevoeld voor het geluk van mijn moeder’
data.description: Met haar essay Project Rust opent Suzanna Jansen een onderzoek naar rusthuizen voor „overspannen” huisvrouwen in de jaren vijftig en zestig. Ook haar moeder bracht er een paar weken door. „Ik kan nu laten zien: het was géén individuele kwestie.”
data.translatedTitle: Suzanna Jansen: 'I have always felt a great responsibility for my mother's happiness'
data.translatedDescription: With her essay Project Rust, Suzanna Jansen opens an investigation into retirement homes for "overstressed" housewives in the 1950s and 1960s. Her mother also spent a few weeks there. “I can now show: it was not an individual matter.”

data.title: Alleen met echt leiderschap kan Jetten zijn kabinet redden

data.translatedTitle: Only with real leadership can Jetten save his cabinet
data.translatedDescription: The leap into the dark that Rob Jetten made by entering into a minority cabinet without an agreement with opposition parties continues. Only with real leadership can the very first D66 prime minister save his cabinet, argues Kemal Rijken.

data.translatedDescription: In Hungary there is not only euphoria about the defeat earlier this year of the autocrat Viktor Orbán, Mandula van den Berg notices when she returns to Budapest for the first time after his fall. Not even among his opponents.

data.title: Het debuut van een AI-actrice op het toneel prikkelt, maar mist diepgang
data.description: In de voorstelling ‘AI&IK’ onderzoekt Eran Ben-Michaël of een vriendschap met AI mogelijk is. De mix van stand-upcomedy en gesprekken met zijn zelfgebouwde AI-model zorgen voor een interessante insteek, maar een diepzinnigere uitwerking had niet misstaan.
data.translatedTitle: The debut of an AI actress on stage is exciting, but lacks depth
data.translatedDescription: In the performance 'AI&IK', Eran Ben-Michaël investigates whether a friendship with AI is possible. The mix of stand-up comedy and conversations with his self-built AI model provides an interesting approach, but a more in-depth elaboration would not have been out of place.

data.title: Annie M.G. Schmidt is ‘van iedereen’ – en haar geboortehuis in het Zeeuwse Kapelle straks ook
data.description: In Kapelle, haar Zeeuwse geboortedorp, is Annie M.G. Schmidt nooit ver weg. De stichting Bij Annie Thuis geeft het huis waarin de kinderboekenschrijfster opgroeide een nieuwe bestemming: een ontmoetingsplek waar haar werk en buurtbewoners samenkomen.
data.translatedTitle: Annie M.G. Schmidt belongs to everyone – and soon so will her birthplace in Kapelle, Zeeland
data.translatedDescription: In Kapelle, her native village in Zeeland, Annie M.G. Schmidt never far away. The Bij Annie Thuis foundation is giving the house in which the children's book author grew up a new purpose: a meeting place where her work and local residents come together.

data.title: Nieuwe koers Groninger Museum: weg van de blockbusters, terug naar het experiment
data.description: De nieuwe opstelling van het Groninger Museum, die dit weekend opent, wil „een nieuw hoofdstuk” zijn, zegt artistiek directeur Roos Gortzak. Het museum was afgelopen jaren artistiek en financieel in zwaar weer terecht gekomen. Blockbusters? Nee, juist niet. „De Groningers hebben lef en moed.”
data.translatedTitle: New course Groninger Museum: away from the blockbusters, back to the experiment
data.translatedDescription: The new arrangement of the Groninger Museum, which opens this weekend, aims to be "a new chapter", says artistic director Roos Gortzak. The museum had found itself in dire straits artistically and financially in recent years. Blockbusters? No, not exactly. “The people of Groningen have courage and courage.”

data.title: ‘Er was een periode waarin werken doorging tot na middernacht, maar nu stop ik uiterlijk om elf uur’

He now works sixty hours a week. She works three days and is following a training course. They share the care of three children.

Sometimes because of security considerations or logistical feasibility, sometimes because the defense does not want to give up a location.

data.translatedTitle: Henk Schiffmacher: 'Take off your shirt and I'll tell you who you are' | Tattoo artist

data.description: De vriendin van mijn moeder is dood. Ze kenden elkaar al sinds de hbs in Rotterdam, dus daarom kende ik haar ook mijn hele leven. De vriendin was orthopedisch schoenmaker.
data.translatedTitle: I know that people often talk scornfully about women with backpacks. Unjustly
data.translatedDescription: My mother's friend is dead. They had known each other since high school in Rotterdam, so that's why I knew her all my life. The girlfriend was an orthopedic shoemaker.

data.description: In Limburg worden op diverse plaatsen monumenten voor zwarte Amerikaanse bevrijders geplaatst. Ze vormen een reactie op het weghalen van informatiepanelen over de militairen op de Amerikaanse begraafplaats in Margraten, wat tot brede ophef leidde.
data.translatedTitle: The old panels were removed, but now the black liberators will have new monuments in Limburg

data.title: Rolex mit Mondphase, Hublot mit Jeff Koons: Der Uhrenherbst bringt einige Überraschungen

data.title: KOMMENTAR - Trump entlarvt die Show von Big Tech – auch Bern und Berlin sollten sich nicht blenden lassen

data.translatedTitle: GASTKOMMENTAR - Europäische Zentralbank: vier Präsidenten, drei Schritte in die falsche Richtung

data.title: Die Wahlen im Nordosten Deutschlands sind auch ein Votum über Bundeskanzler Friedrich Merz
data.description: In Berlin und Mecklenburg-Vorpommern dürfte die AfD ihre Wähleranteile erneut deutlich steigern, auch wenn die Partei keine Regierungsbeteiligung erhält. Für CDU und SPD steht viel auf dem Spiel.

data.title: KOMMENTAR - Ursula von der Leyens Schwäche: Sie erfindet ständig Neues, statt Bestehendes durchzusetzen
data.description: Diese Woche hat die EU-Kommissions-Präsidentin ein komplexes Gesetz zu sozialen Netzwerken vorgestellt. Zudem möchte sie Kanada als «assoziiertes Mitglied» in die EU aufnehmen. Wer ständig so visionär denkt, scheitert fast zwangsläufig.
data.translatedTitle: KOMMENTAR - Ursula von der Leyens Schwäche: Sie erfindet ständig Neues, statt Bestehendes durchzusetzen
data.translatedDescription: This week the President of the EU Commission presented a complex law on social networks. She would also like to admit Canada to the EU as an “associated member”. Anyone who constantly thinks in such a visionary way will almost inevitably fail.

data.title: Baut Iran sein Atomprogramm wieder auf? Neue Satellitenbilder zeigen verdächtige Aktivitäten
data.description: Teheran renoviert eine Militäranlage, die im Zusammenhang mit dem Nuklearprogramm steht und schon zweimal bombardiert wurde. Ob die Iraner Atomwaffen derzeit wirklich herstellen können, ist aber fraglich. Nun droht Donald Trump erneut mit Angriffen.
data.translatedTitle: Baut Iran sein Atomprogramm wieder auf? Neue Satellitenbilder zeigen verdächtige Aktivitäten
data.translatedDescription: Tehran is renovating a military facility linked to its nuclear program that has already been bombed twice. However, it is questionable whether the Iranians can currently actually produce nuclear weapons. Now Donald Trump is threatening attacks again.

data.title: Trotz Sanktionen schickt Nordkorea Arbeiter ins Ausland – und verdient so bis zu 800 Millionen Dollar

data.translatedDescription: The number of North Korean workers is increasing sharply, especially in Russia. Most of their income goes to the Kim regime.

data.translatedTitle: INTERVIEW - “Greed is the central deadly sin of sport,” says a philosopher. Gianni Infantino and Jürgen Klopp are both greedy – in different ways
