data.title: Romania’s PM-designate begins work on governing programme, says priorities will be presented next week
data.description: Romanian prime minister-designate Siegfried Mureșan said on Friday, September 18, that he was ready to form a “serious, reform-oriented, and pro-European” government. He announced that experts from the three parties backing him - the National Liberal Party (PNL), Save Romania Union (USR), and the Democratic Alliance of Hungarians in Romania (UDMR) - would “immediately begin drafting a governing programme.” Mureșan, a member of the European Parliament, said his priorities would be presented at the beginning of next week, after which negotiations would be held with members of Parliament. “I am prepared to form a serious, reform-oriented, pro-European government that presents an agenda for modernizing Romania, reflected in a higher standard of living and good measures for the people,” he told journalists at the Parliament. He added that Romania needed a credible government as soon as possible to continue reforms and projects launched over the past year. “The most important thing is what we will do for the country from the first day this government is invested,” he said. “We will be extremely transparent at every stage of this process.” In his turn, present at the same press conference, interim prime minister and PNL leader Ilie Bolojan said his party and experts from the ministries would provide the data needed for Siegfried Mureșan to develop his programme. “The responsibility is the same as it was three months ago: to form a government,” Bolojan said. He listed maintaining fiscal stability, ensuring the operation of the state and public services, preparing next year’s budget, and creating conditions for economic recovery among the main priorities. Meanwhile, USR leader Dominic Fritz said his party supported Siegfried Mureșan because it considered him the right person to restore public confidence during a period of political and economic tension. “We intend to form a serious and coherent government with a vision based on trust,” Fritz said. He further added that USR would also be open to discussions with the Social Democratic Party (PSD) to ensure a Parliament majority for the future government. PNL, USR and UDMR together hold 169 of the 233 votes required for investiture. Even with all 17 votes from the national minorities group, they would reach only 186, leaving Mureșan to secure another 47 votes. Also present at the press conference on Friday, representing UDMR, Tánczos Barna said the objective should be a stable government able to remain in office until 2028. He argued that rebuilding the majority that collapsed in April, potentially under a rotating premiership arrangement, could still be the best option but would require talks with PSD. “We emphasize that we will not participate in forming any government that requires the support of AUR, SOS Romania or other extremist formations,” Barna said. President Nicușor Dan proposed Siegfried Mureșan for prime minister on Thursday following almost six hours of consultations with parliamentary parties. The Liberal MEP accepted the proposal shortly afterwards. Dan said he would sign the nomination decree in Bistrița on Saturday, with its publication in the Official Gazette scheduled for Monday, according to News.ro . Asked about Mureșan’s prospects of securing a majority, the president acknowledged that the task would be difficult but said he wanted him to succeed. PSD called on Siegfried Mureșan to present his plans publicly and explain whether he intended to continue or change the policies of the Ilie Bolojan government. The Social Democrats said discussions about parliamentary votes should follow the presentation of the governing programme and measures for the population. Romania has been governed by Ilie Bolojan’s caretaker administration since his Liberal-led cabinet was dismissed in a no-confidence vote more than four months ago. If Siegfried Mureșan’s proposed cabinet fails to win Parliament’s confidence, it would be the second rejected investiture request, potentially opening the way for the president to consider dissolving Parliament and calling early elections.

data.title: Local release date announced for Romania’s Oscar pick Fjord
data.description: Cristian Mungiu’s film Fjord , which earned him the second Palme d’Or of his career and has been selected as Romania’s entry for the 2027 Academy Awards, will have its local premiere on January 15, 2027. The release will be marked by a gala screening at Bucharest’s Sala Palatului, attended by the director, actors Sebastian Stan and Renate Reinsve, as well as other members of the cast and crew. Before its January premiere, Fjord will be shown in Romania as part of a nationwide special screening organized during the festival Les Films de Cannes à Bucarest on October 24. The film will be screened simultaneously at all participating cinemas in Bucharest and across the country. Tickets for the special screening will go on sale on October 1. The screening will be followed by a conversation between director Cristian Mungiu and the public. Fjord will premiere in the United States on October 9. Before the U.S. awards season begins, the movie will be released in theaters in more than 40 countries. “I’m pleased that Fjord has got off to a good start in America and that several prestigious publications have included us on their lists of Oscar favorites in multiple categories. This is an opportunity that Romanian cinema has never had before, given the costs of running a promotional campaign in the United States. I’m receiving a great deal of encouragement from Romanians at home and abroad who want to see an Oscar for Romania. I assure them that the greatest support they can offer us is to go and see the film when it is released in cinemas in their countries,” Cristian Mungiu said, quoted by Agerpres . To coincide with the film’s U.S. premiere in October, New York and Los Angeles will host a photography exhibition by director Cristian Mungiu, featuring images captured in Norway during the preparation and filming of Fjord . The exhibition can also currently be viewed in Bucharest at Art Safari.

data.title: Construction works up 11% in Romania in first seven months of 2026
data.description: The volume of construction works rose in July 2026 compared with June 2026 by 7.6% in gross terms and by 1.4% in seasonally and working-day-adjusted terms. Compared with July 2025, it increased by 2.0% as a gross series, while as a series adjusted for the number of working days and seasonality, it decreased by 8.3%. July 2026 compared with June 2026 In July 2026, compared with June 2026, the volume of construction works increased, as a gross series, by 7.6%, with increases recorded in maintenance and current repairs works (9.2%), capital repairs works (7.3%) and new construction works (7.2%). By type of construction, increases were recorded in non-residential buildings (11.4%), residential buildings (9.0%) and engineering construction works (5.3%). As a series adjusted for the number of working days and seasonality, the volume of construction works increased by 1.4%, with increases recorded in maintenance and current repairs works (7.3%), new construction works (4.1%) and capital repairs works (2.7%). By type of construction, the volume of construction works increased in non-residential buildings (9.0%), residential buildings (3.9%) and engineering construction works (1.6%). July 2026 compared with July 2025 In July 2026, compared with July 2025, the volume of construction works, as a gross series, increased overall by 2.0%. By structural elements, an increase was recorded in new construction works (6.4%), while capital repair works and maintenance and current repair works decreased by 8.7% and 3.2%, respectively. By type of construction, increases were recorded in residential buildings (10.8%) and non-residential buildings (1.3%), while engineering construction decreased by 0.5%. As a series adjusted for the number of working days and seasonality, the volume of construction works decreased overall by 8.3%. By structural elements, decreases were recorded in capital repair works (11.8%) and maintenance and current repair works (5.1%). New construction works increased by 4.6%. By type of construction, the volume of construction works increased in residential buildings (9.6%) and non-residential buildings (0.2%), while engineering construction decreased by 2.4%. January-July 2026 compared with January-July 2025 The INS said that in the period January 1-July 31, 2026, compared with the same period in 2025, the volume of construction works, as a gross series, increased overall by 11.2%, with increases recorded in new construction works (14.2%), maintenance and current repairs works (7.0%) and capital repairs works (4.0%). By type of construction, increases were recorded in residential buildings (18.6%), engineering construction (10.6%) and non-residential buildings (7.5%). At the same time, the volume of construction works increased, as a series adjusted for the number of working days and seasonality, by 8.2%, with increases recorded in new construction works (13.4%), maintenance and current repair works (6.3%), and capital repair works (2.9%). By type of construction, increases were recorded in residential buildings (17.9%), engineering construction (8.4%), and non-residential buildings (7.2%), according to INS data.

data.title: Romanian-British artist Cristina Schek returns to London’s W4th Plinth
data.description: Romanian-British artist Cristina Schek will unveil her monumental work Fern Girl at W4th Plinth in west London on Saturday, September 19. The 4-by-4-metre piece will be displayed on the railway embankment wall at Turnham Green Terrace in Chiswick, the Romanian Cultural Institute (ICR) in London announced. Created in 2022 at the intersection of photography and digital art, Fern Girl depicts a female figure almost absorbed by vegetation. Leaves become clothing, camouflage and a second skin, blurring the boundary between the human body and nature. “I love the idea that Fern Girl will live for several months in the middle of London, on a four-metre wall,” Cristina Schek said. “People do not enter a gallery to see the work; the work appears on their way to the station, home, or their morning coffee.” Supported by the Romanian Cultural Institute in London, the installation makes Schek the only artist in the project’s history to present two separate works. Her first W4th Plinth piece, The Ceiling in the Sky, was unveiled in 2023 by British actress Dame Siân Phillips. Fern Girl was selected in a 2022 competition that attracted almost 500 submissions. It will be officially unveiled at 14:00 by art historian Cynthia Valianti Corbett, founder of the Cynthia Corbett Gallery and the Young Masters Art Prize. “In Fern Girl , I play with logic again: this time, the ferns have taken control, and the vegetation and the human figure are no longer quite sure where one ends and the other begins,” Cristina Schek said. Five days after the unveiling, the artist’s works will also be presented at the British Art Fair at London’s Saatchi Gallery. She is due to participate in Art Miami in the United States in December. Cristina Schek is a London-based Romanian-British visual artist whose practice combines photography, digital manipulation, surrealism, and visual storytelling. Inspired by the Fourth Plinth in Trafalgar Square, W4th Plinth was launched in 2019 with a work by British artist Sir Peter Blake. Curated by environmental and educational organization Abundance London, the project displays large-scale contemporary art in public spaces, with works generally remaining in place for at least six months.

data.title: Romanian government greenlights Braşov–Făgăraş Highway project
data.description: Representatives of the Ministry of Transport said that the Braşov-Făgăraş Highway will contribute to improving national and regional connectivity for road traffic by providing a fast connection between the municipalities of Braşov and Făgăraş, respectively, and Sibiu, given that this highway section will connect with the Făgăraş–Sibiu Highway section. According to the draft government decision , the investment is estimated at RON 9.35 billion (including VAT), while the construction period is 36 months. The investment value is significant, and the funding will be provided from European funds, through the Transport Programme 2021–2027, as well as from the state budget, through the budget of the Ministry of Transport and Infrastructure, within the limits of the amounts approved annually for this purpose. After several analyses, the designers established a route with a length of 49.75 km and a platform width of 26 meters, according to Bună Ziua Brașov . Along its route, 46 bridges, passages or viaducts will be built, a set of service areas (one in each direction), a set of parking areas (one in each direction), a maintenance and coordination center, as well as an interchange. The project also provides for the construction of six tunnel-type structures and cut-and-cover/overpasses. The new highway will occupy a total area of 663 hectares (public and private land) and will pass through the territories of the localities of Codlea, Dumbrăviţa, Şercaia, Şinca, and Mândra. The interchange designed along this highway section will be built at Şercaia, where the maintenance and coordination center will also be located. This interchange will provide a connection with DN 1 (Braşov–Sibiu), as well as with DN 1S (Şercaia–Hoghiz). It will therefore connect three highways, namely Braşov–Comarnic (through the Codlea–Cristian section), Braşov–Sibiu and Braşov–Bacău.

data.title: Coffee ecosystem app developed in Romania raises funding from TechAngels, Food Angels Hub investors
data.description: Brewtifi, an app for specialty coffee enthusiasts and businesses across the coffee ecosystem, has secured funding from a group of angel investors from the TechAngels and Food Angels Hub networks. Following the investment, with an undisclosed value, Brewtifi has reached a valuation of approximately EUR 1.6 million, less than a year after its launch, the company said. The round was led on behalf of TechAngels by Mălin Ștefănescu and on behalf of Food Angels Hub by entrepreneur Radu Savopol, the co-founder of the 5 to go group. The funding round will support the acceleration of the company’s product and business plans, the expansion of its community, and “strengthening of the app’s position as a go-to platform for discovering quality coffee, coffee shops, events, and communities dedicated to coffee lovers across Europe.” Launched in October 2025, the Brewtifi app currently has more than 20,000 users across Europe. The app features more than 8,500 specialty coffee shops and over 180 coffee roasters across Europe, allowing users to discover specialty coffee, new places, brands, and events relevant to the coffee community. “This funding brings together people with experience in both technology and the food& beverage industry. For Brewtifi, their support means more than just capital: it also provides know-how, validation, and access to valuable perspectives on scaling, product development, and community building. Together, we want to build a platform that connects coffee enthusiasts with the places, roasteries, communities, and experiences worth discovering,” Brewtifi representatives said. “I look forward to the moment when I can tell my children over a coffee how happy I am that I invested in Brewtifi from the very beginning. Either way, I’m sure we’ll be proud to have been part of this story, which started here and of which we are now a part,” Mălin Ștefănescu said. “What I appreciate about BREWTIFI is precisely the way it connects coffee lovers with what’s available on the market and encourages this growing desire to explore. There are so many places where you can have great coffee-related experiences, and I believe it’s important to make them easier to find. I think that’s what Brewtifi does: it brings consumers, coffee shops, and brands closer together,” Radu Savopol said. The transaction received legal assistance from law firm Andronic and Partners.

data.title: Western Romania: former Timiș prefect detained by EPPO for allegedly defrauding EU funds
data.description: Prosecutors from the body headed by famed Romanian prosecutor Codruța Kovesi picked up the former prefect and took her into custody. Five other people suspected of fraud involving EU funds have also been taken in by prosecutors in this case, according to DeBanat.ro . The scandal began on June 12, when prosecutors and police officers conducted searches at Micicoi’s home. The investigation looked into the use of European funds to organize training courses for disadvantaged people. Specifically, police analyzed a project carried out through the local action group Freidorf, in which the association headed by the prefect at the time was involved. According to judicial sources, the damages caused are in the hundreds of thousands of euros. Micicoi claimed that she had no capacity in the case and that she was innocent of any wrongdoing. “These are procedural checks, in a case in which I do not even have the status of witness, I have not been summoned, and no accusations have been brought to my attention by the investigative authorities. There was no premise for me to possess or fail to provide documents necessary for the investigation,” Micicoi said on June 12. That same day, under public and party pressure, she decided to resign from the position of prefect, to which she had been appointed by the center-right Save Romania Union, or USR, in October of 2025. The party is well-known for its hardline anti-corruption stance.

data.title: Romania: a strategic choice for investors. 30 years of French-Romanian partnership: the way forward
data.description: Over 4,200 companies with majority French capital operate on the local market, generating approximately 125,000 jobs. The French presence spans nearly all key economic sectors: the automotive and manufacturing industries, energy, financial services, retail, IT, aeronautics, agriculture, and construction. Beyond the figures, these investments have brought new technologies, expertise, and working standards that have contributed to the modernization of the Romanian business environment. 30 years of commercial bonds and progress We live today in a world vastly different from the one we knew thirty years ago. The evolution has been systemic, encompassing the transition from a closed economy to a market economy, Romania's accession to the EU and transatlantic structures, and the natural evolution of society alongside technological advancements such as the advent of the internet, large-scale telecommunications, digitalization, AI, and workflow automation. All these developments place Romania firmly on investors' radars today, particularly given the structural competitive advantages already mentioned. The Romanian economy has reached maturity, driven primarily by the professionalism fostered through the exchange of expertise between local human capital and the experience brought by investors from mature markets. Foreign investment, the absorption of European funds, and the adoption of professional standards have all contributed to a process of widespread progress. "We are also witnessing a shift in the investment paradigm: a transition from the low-cost/best-cost model toward one focused on added value. This shift is possible precisely because the market has matured and is capable of delivering high-end services and added value, rather than merely supplying raw materials or low-cost labor." said Nicolas Richard, President of CCIFER. 100% trust in Romania According to a study conducted by CCIFER in April 2026, which received about 100 answers from C-level executives of the member companies, when asked if they still see their business developing in Romania, 100% of the respondents stated YES. "Therefore, the strongest message of the community is that Romania is a strategic bet, even amidst a context marked by geopolitical uncertainty, budgetary pressure, and legislative volatility."* said Adriana Record, Executive Director of CCIFER. How to attract more investors from France The most significant obstacles to Romania's development are identified in the same study mentioned above as being mostly at an institutional level: political instability, legislative unpredictability, bureaucracy, corruption, insufficient administrative capacity, and the lack of a long-term strategic vision. However, Romania continues to benefit from key structural advantages: competitive human capital, membership in the European Union and NATO, a favorable geostrategic position, and significant competitive potential in sectors such as energy, industry, agriculture, and technology. As perceived by the CCIFER community, the way to maintain investors' appetite is to continue capitalizing on the structural competitive advantages also identified in the study. First and foremost, Romania's membership in the European community and NATO represents a strategic competitive advantage over other countries in the region. Another extremely valuable strategic resource, recognized by all respondents as an absolute competitive advantage, is human capital: highly talented individuals who are eager to learn, resilient in the face of current challenges, and solution-oriented. Economic sectors with competitive potential and an impact on regional security, such as energy, represent another strategic factor. In the meantime, while maximizing strengths, it is also important to tackle the key identified barriers to economic development: political instability, legislative unpredictability, bureaucracy, corruption, insufficient administrative capacity, and the lack of a long-term strategic vision. By supporting and intensifying dialogue between public institutions and the business community, public policies become more aligned with economic realities, a role CCIFER has played in Romania for 30 years through dedicated sessions, sector-specific events, and community-generated position papers. Foster sustained joint efforts, such as the partnership CCIFER has conducted in education with the country's dual education institutions and the university sector, aimed at bridging the gap between actual labor market needs and the skills acquired in schools, while also actively identifying career opportunities for young graduates. Leverage on public-private partnership projects and a coherent regulatory framework for such initiatives can serve as a strategic solution to address the identified challenges. Looking towards the next 30 years "Looking ahead for the next thirty years, the CCIFER community envisions a prosperous, modern, European Romania and, above all, a place that feels like home: a place where people choose to stay. In this context, CCIFER embraces the role of a key player in fostering cohesion and influence, and in facilitating dialogue between the business community and the authorities."* said Nicolas Richard, President of CCIFER. As it enters its fourth decade of activity, CCIFER aims to continue expanding its community, with a strong focus on SMEs and regional development, to help build the skills of the future, and to intensify dialogue with authorities on key issues such as taxation, infrastructure, the reduction of bureaucracy, and digitalization. Romania possesses valuable assets: talent, creativity, a strategic location, and significant potential in sectors such as energy, agriculture, industry, and technology. The challenge lies no longer in identifying opportunities, but in creating a coherent framework that allows them to be fully leveraged. For 30 years, this has been the core objective of the conversation CCIFER conducts with its partners: to contribute to building a more competitive and sustainable economy.

data.title: Trump’s UNGA Schedule Omits Bilateral Meeting With Zelensky
data.description: President Volodymyr Zelensky is not included among the leaders scheduled to hold bilateral meetings with US President Donald Trump at the UN General Assembly in New York. Two senior Ukrainian officials confirmed that no meeting is currently finalized. Trump’s announced itinerary includes addresses to the UNGA and bilateral meetings with UK Prime Minister Andy Burnham, Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi, GCC leaders, and acting Venezuelan President Delcy Rodríguez before returning to Washington on Tuesday evening.

data.title: Russian Strike on Kharkiv Region Kills 4

Rescuers initially recovered an elderly couple from beneath the debris before the death toll rose to four on Saturday morning.

data.title: South Korea Signs Pact With EU on Satellite Network
data.description: South Korea signed an administrative agreement with the European Commission on Thursday to explore future integration with the EU’s flagship IRIS² secure satellite constellation. European Defence and Space Commissioner Andrius Kubilius and South Korean defense officials confirmed that a joint working group will evaluate system-level cooperation between Korea’s sovereign K-LEO program and IRIS², an orbital network designed as a European sovereign alternative to Starlink.

data.title: Switzerland Adopts Security Strategy to Counter Hybrid Threats
data.description: The Swiss government has adopted a comprehensive new security strategy featuring 10 objectives and 46 concrete measures to reinforce national defense capabilities, protect critical infrastructure, and prepare against hybrid and standoff attacks. Formulated amid Europe’s deteriorating security environment driven by Russia’s war against Ukraine, the framework emphasizes pre-arranged defense cooperation mechanisms with international partner states.

data.title: US Approves $2.68B Air Defense Equipment Sale to Ukraine
data.description: The US Department of State approved a potential $2.68 billion Foreign Military Sale to Ukraine for air defense development upgrades, equipment, and services on Sept. 18. The package includes S-300 Clone missiles, GAM-67 missiles, range-extended laser-guided rockets, ITEL 1.5 launchers, and RPS 202 counter-drone radars. The procurement will be financed through European partner contributions and previously appropriated US Foreign Military Financing credited to the Ukraine Reconstruction Investment Fund.

data.title: Russia’s Shadow Fleet Shipments from Baltic Ports Rise 10.1%, KSE Institute Says
data.description: KSE Institute estimates that Russia exported around 5.3 mb/d of crude oil and oil products by sea in July 2026, down 10.7% m-o-m and 6.4% y-o-y. Of 268 tankers used, 150, or 56%, were shadow fleet vessels; 93% of shadow tankers were over 15 years old. Shadow fleet shipments from Baltic Sea ports rose 10.1% m-o-m and 21.2% y-o-y.

data.description: Ukraine’s annual consumer and core inflation both stood at 8.1% in August. Fuel and water tariffs drove costs higher, while the new harvest lowered food prices. The central bank expects damage to logistics infrastructure to add to inflation through the autumn.

data.title: New Duma: Do the Russians Have a Choice?
data.description: Russia’s three-day parliamentary elections will elect the 450-member Duma, regional lawmakers and governors. data.title: Ukraine Drones Make Orchestrating Russia’s Elections Tougher

data.title: DSP o Maquiavélico Ganancioso
data.description: Guineenses, mais uma vez, venho para vos alertar sobre o perigo que Domingos Simões Pereira representa para a Guiné-Bissau. Faço esse alerta a todos os guineenses sem exceção que se encontre no país ou no estrangeiro, ao PAIGC em especial e na pessoa do Cipriano Cassamá em concreto. Alerta esse sobre o verdadeiro DSP, o verdadeiro espírito que move esse sujeito, o qual alguns ainda continuam a acreditar para não dizer adorar. Domingos Simões Pereira é um manipulador, um verdadeiro chantagista e calculista provavelmente, tipo de comportamento que ultrapassa o nível de psicopata. U m ambicioso desmedido, um verdadeiro criminoso que sabe como e quando cometer o crime. Ele jamais coabitaria não só com JOMAV, assim como com qualquer presidente que seria eleito, a não ser o que ele apoiou disfarçadamente. Isto porque ele tem sua própria agenda, e o PAIGC é simplesmente uma plataforma para sua concretização. DSP jamais coabitaria com JOMAV porque o seu candidato preferido era o Paulo Gomes e sempre será, o qual juntamente com Tchitchi vão delineando mecanismo de modo a serem os novos donos da Guiné-Bissau. Segundo eles este é um processo a médio prazo, e é preciso coragem e paciência para concretiza-lo. Ganhar o congresso não importa em que circunstância e ter novamente o partido na mão, é uma fase concluída em proveito deles, enquanto verdadeiros militantes do PAIGC estão a bater palmas. Depois dessa eleição legislativa, não importa o resultado, o Cipriano Cassama que se prepare a mala ou fica de bico fechado, pois o candidato preferido para o partido será o Paulo Gomes, e esse sim deve ter a voz dentro do partido. data.title: DSP, UM PERIGO GRAVE PARA FUTURO DO PAÍS
data.description: Os meios de comunicação também são as formas de manipulação mais utilizadas pelos poderes políticos, dado o seu impacto social. As informações são manipuladas não apenas tendo em vista omitir factos relevantes, mas também distorcer o conteúdo da informação veiculada, produzir ou forjar a opinião pública, de modo que a mesma se ajuste às ideias dos gananciosos. A única forma dos cidadãos evitarem cair nestes processos de manipulação é tornarem-se mais vigilantes em relação às instituições democráticas e aos órgãos de informação, adoptando uma atitude de permanente reflexão crítica sobre a informação que lhes é fornecida. Na Guiné-Bissau, nos últimos anos, cresceu exponencialmente o número de pessoas mediocres, pessoas sem escrúpulos ligadas à produção de rádios e outros meios de comunicação com influencia na nossa sociedade, gente que apesar da sua enorme influência na sociedade, trabalha na mais completa impunidade e sem qualquer controlo ético/democrático. Obcecado pelo poder, ciente da dificuldade do povo guineense em avaliar informações, ciente do poder dos instrumentos de comunicação, Domingos Simões Pereira (DSP) nunca menosprezou esses instrumentos para atingir seu objectivo, sempre usou-os de forma desonesta como agora está a fazer tudo por tudo para manter no controlo desses veicúlos, mesmo que isso custe a vida dos outros. Governou na corrupção, no nepotismo e no desvios de somas astronómicas do dinheiro de povo, que muito serviria para investimentos na saúde, educação e outros serviços publicos, para beneficiar familiares e amigos. Finge que preocupa com os problemas do país, mas só engana o povo honesto, humilde e trabalhador que infelizmente sofre muito, não sei até quando, devido a sua paciência e tolerância aos governantes como DSP, criminoso travestido em politico que vive na custa de povo e acima de tudo ainda fa-lo refem do próprio suor. Roubou e decepcionou tanto não só aos guineenses assim como a comunidade internacional que sempre acreditou que o sujeito era ideal para ajudar esse povo a sair do ciclo de sofrimento que parece infinito. Foi demitido, não conformou e está a fazer tudo na medida do possível para continuar a complicar a vida dos guineenses. Razão disso é que depois de perder a batalha nos meios de comunicações mais modernos nomeadamente os blogues onde investiu grandes somas do dinheiro de povo, para fazer a lavagem cerebral dos menos instruídos e não só. Fugiu do facebook onde sempre frequentava e comunicava com todos tentado passar a mensagem de um politico moderno e aberto a diálogo/opiniões, mas que afinal era simplesmente um falso modernista. Caiu a mascara e já não consegue enganar ninguem, pois a sua credibilidade está abaixo de zero, para não dizer outra coisa. Camaradas, para conhecimento geral, com o dinheiro roubado que custou suor de povo guineense, DSP decidiu avançar com um outro novo plano maquiavelico, para criar a sua própria estação de rádio.
